If the inheritance pattern is autosomal dominant or X-linked, the disease gene is likely found on double-stranded DNA in the nucleus, as both types of genes are located there. In contrast, if a mitochondrial inheritance pattern is noted, the disease gene would be located on circular DNA in the mitochondrion. Cytoplasmic inheritance is unlikely based on the pedigree, indicating that the disease gene is not found on single-stranded DNA or RNA in the cytoplasm. Therefore, the most likely locations for the disease gene, depending on the inheritance pattern, are either on double-stranded DNA in the nucleus or on circular DNA in the mitochondrion.
